issues.legal_issue: A decree for specific performance requires a valid and enforceable contract whose material terms are certain and on which the parties reached agreement.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought specific performance of a written entry said to record an agreement to sell property and machinery, while the defendant disputed that the agreement covered the building and other parts of the property.
The parties’ correspondence reflected differing understandings of what was to be sold, including whether the building was included.
The entry did not clearly identify the land, define the vendor’s share if the co-owner did not join in the sale, or specify the price for that share.
The terms of an alleged preceding oral agreement were not proved.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff did not establish a valid and enforceable contract on agreed and sufficiently certain terms, so specific performance was unavailable; the appeal was dismissed and the refund decree was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Specific performance enforces the obligation actually undertaken, so the contract’s terms must be certain and the parties must have reached consensus ad idem; the plaintiff bears the burden of proving those terms and that agreement. A court cannot make a contract for the parties. Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 permits a defendant to raise any defence available under contract law. The court also described specific-performance jurisdiction as discretionary, drawing on Fry’s Specific Performance, 6th ed., and Halsbury’s Laws of England; no earlier judicial decision was relied on for this holding.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A party brought a proceeding seeking an order requiring another party to perform an alleged contract.
predicates.material_terms_uncertain: The alleged agreement left material matters, such as the property to be transferred, the share to be transferred, or the consideration, unresolved.
predicates.parties_lacked_matching_understanding: The parties’ accounts or communications showed that they understood the subject or terms of the alleged transaction differently.
predicates.specific_performance_unavailable_for_no_: The court does not order specific performance because no valid and enforceable contract on sufficiently certain, mutually agreed terms was established.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance proceeding concerns an alleged agreement with uncertain material terms or no matching understanding between the parties, the output is that specific performance is unavailable for want of an enforceable contract.

issues.legal_issue: When an agreement makes performance conditional on a co-owner joining in a sale and also provides for repayment if that does not occur, the repayment may be an alternative to performance rather than a basis for compelling a sale of the promisor’s share.
material_facts: The written entry provided that if the co-owner did not sign the sale deed, the promisor would sell her own share, otherwise repay the advance with compensation in the same amount, and the buyer could take the advance.
The co-owner refused to sell her share.
The entry did not clearly define the promisor’s share or the consideration for its sale.
issues.conclusion: The repayment language could be construed as an alternative to performance; if the promisor chose that alternative, there was no breach of an obligation to sell, and specific performance could not be ordered on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Where a promise is framed in alternatives and one alternative becomes impossible, whether the promisor must perform the remaining alternative or is excused depends on the parties’ intention ascertained from the contract’s nature and terms and the circumstances. A contract may give a party the option to perform an act or instead pay a specified sum. The court relied on Halsbury’s Laws of England, 4th ed., vol. 9, para. 446, and vol. 44, para. 417; no earlier judicial decision was relied on for this holding.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A party brought a proceeding seeking an order requiring another party to perform an alleged contract.
predicates.coowner_refused_to_join: A co-owner whose participation was contemplated in the transaction declined to join in the transfer.
predicates.agreement_provided_refund_alternative: The alleged agreement provided for repayment or payment as an alternative if the contemplated transfer could not proceed.
predicates.promisor_may_choose_refund_instead_of_pe: The promisor may select the payment alternative, in which case specific performance of the contemplated transfer is not ordered on that basis.

issues.definition: If a specific-performance proceeding involves a co-owner who refused to join and an agreement providing a refund alternative, the output is that the promisor may choose the refund instead of performance.
